mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or positive returns occur in less than 55% of high PAYEMS periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.5%, the S&P 500 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an expansionary economic cycle with accommodative monetary policy, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of rising INDPRO and falling FEDFUNDS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals an impending Federal Reserve tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of residential construction (HOUST) indicates strong housing market activity, which is a leading indicator of consumer spending and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 20-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or positive returns occur in less than 55% of high HOUST periods.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.0% signals monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in residential sales and financial services (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust consumer demand and economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of rising RSAFS and rising INDPRO fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) during a tight labor market boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE is below 4.0%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in less than 60% of cases.
